entries.text: A key provision of this rule determines that demurrage or detention invoices can only be issued to either: (1) the person for whose account the billing party provide ocean transportation or storage of cargo and who contracted with the billing party for the ocean transportation or storage of cargo; or (2) the “consignee,” defined as “the ultimate recipient of the cargo; the person to whom final delivery of the cargo is to be made”. Demurrage and detention bills cannot be issued to multiple parties simultaneously.

The rule also requires vessel-operating-common carriers (VOCCs) and MTOs to issue detention and demurrage invoices within 30 calendar days from when charges were last incurred. Non-vessel-operating common carriers must issue demurrage and detention invoices within 30 calendar days from the issuance date of the invoice they received.

Billed parties have at least 30 calendar days to make fee mitigation, refund, or waiver requests. If a timely filed request is made, the billing party must attempt to resolve the matter within 30 calendar days, unless both parties agree to a longer timeframe.

The new rule will advance the Commission’s goal of promoting supply chain fluidity by ensuring a clear connection between the failure to pick-up cargo or return equipment in a timely manner and the appropriate fee. The rule ensures that billed parties understand the demurrage or detention invoices they receive by requiring certain identifiable information be included by the billing party on the invoice. Failing to include any of the required information in a detention or demurrage invoice eliminates any obligation of the billed party to pay the applicable charge. Of course, if an invoice does comply, a charged party does have an obligation to pay charges billed. The new rule will provide relief to parties who should never have received a bill for detention or demurrage.

These data are provided to the FMC, summarized, and then made available to the public for a general understanding of the scope of detention and demurrage billed by and paid to carriers. Detention is charged for extended use of intermodal equipment and demurrage accrues when a container exceeds free time on a marine terminal.

# Development Brief

## Original Need

Create a resettable synthetic ocean-container demurrage and detention invoice dispute environment that represents realistic actors, invoices, containers, charge periods, and supporting evidence.
Model the normal dispute workflow, material timing rules, and observable status transitions.
Refuse invalid or late disputes without prohibited state mutation.
Provide meaningful reproducible initial data without contacting real carrier systems.

## Selected interpretation

A bounded United States synthetic environment centered on a vessel-operating common carrier (VOCC) billing a consignee for import demurrage and detention. The environment uses a fixed synthetic calendar, deterministic seed, fabricated carrier and terminal identities, and local-only state. It models a normal dispute lifecycle with a synthetic 30-calendar-day dispute window and a separate 30-calendar-day resolution target for timely requests. The externally evidenced timing facts are limited to VOCC invoice issuance and the FMC-described request and resolution periods; the exact synthetic dispute-window anchor is a disclosed Need-authorized workflow choice, not a claim that all carriers or jurisdictions use identical commercial rules.

## Atomic Need mapping

### NEED-001 — accepted

Create a resettable synthetic ocean-container demurrage and detention invoice dispute environment that represents realistic actors, invoices, containers, charge periods, and supporting evidence.

Requirements: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-024

The draft represents synthetic actors, invoices, containers, charge periods, supporting evidence, and meaningful initial records.

### NEED-002 — accepted

Model the normal dispute workflow, material timing rules, and observable status transitions.

Requirements: REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-006, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015

The draft defines normal submission, validation, review, resolution, timing rules, and observable status transitions.

### NEED-003 — accepted

Refuse invalid or late disputes without prohibited state mutation.

Requirements: REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-020

The draft defines invalid and late-dispute refusals together with explicit prohibited mutations.

### NEED-004 — accepted

Provide meaningful reproducible initial data without contacting real carrier systems.

Requirements: REQ-012, REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-022, REQ-021

The draft defines reproducible initial data, reset and isolation behavior, synthetic-only execution, and a prohibition on real carrier-system contact.

## Capabilities

### REQ-001

Represent synthetic parties and their relationships, including a VOCC, marine terminal, consignee or billed customer, shipper, trucker, freight forwarder, and dispute analyst. A shipment relates a bill of lading, container, port or terminal events, and the party accountable for the invoice.

Basis: need

Observable: A world inspection exposes fabricated party identifiers, roles, shipment relationships, container ownership or custody relationships, and the single billed party for each invoice.

Falsifiable consequence: A world inspection that cannot identify the billed party or cannot relate an invoice to a shipment and container violates this capability.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-002

Represent invoices with invoice identity, billed party, issue date, due date, currency, total amount, line items, charge type, container number, shipment reference, charge-period dates, free-time dates, rate basis, and an explanation of the amount.

Basis: need

Observable: An invoice view displays each charge line, its container and date range, the applicable free-time interval, daily or tiered rate, calculated amount, and invoice total.

Falsifiable consequence: An invoice with an amount that cannot be traced to a charge line, rate, container, and charge period violates this capability.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-003

Represent demurrage as a charge associated with a container exceeding free time while at a marine terminal, and detention as a charge associated with extended use of intermodal equipment. The selected variant treats free time, chargeable days, and rate tiers as explicit data rather than implicit text.

Basis: need

Observable: A charge-period view identifies whether a line is demurrage or detention, where the container or equipment was situated, the free-time interval, the chargeable interval, and the resulting days and amount.

Falsifiable consequence: A charge line whose type, location or equipment-use basis cannot be distinguished is inconsistent with the selected domain model.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-004

Represent supporting evidence as synthetic records linked to an invoice line or dispute, including bill of lading or sea-waybill data, container availability and release events, terminal-gate or pickup events, empty-return events, appointment records, customs or hold notices, equipment-unavailability notices, and correspondence.

Basis: need

Observable: A dispute can display the evidence items submitted for each disputed line, their timestamps, source role, relationship to the container, and whether they support or contradict the asserted timing.

Falsifiable consequence: A dispute that accepts attachments but cannot associate them with a disputed line, container, or event fails this capability.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-005

The bounded variant permits only one billed party per demurrage or detention invoice and models the consignee as the ultimate recipient of the cargo when that role is used as the billed party.

Basis: external_evidence

Observable: Invoice validation shows exactly one billed party and rejects an invoice configured with simultaneous billing to multiple parties.

Falsifiable consequence: An accepted invoice with two simultaneous billed parties contradicts the selected external rule basis.

Evidence: `E1` -> `source-revision-33fad34d48b676fa9f8d1b415c7f6dcbee67976d84b4302842a4ce4d43e0bd42/passage-2209f389bad3b80f0df0770f9ca6981ade0f2342e1b3cd8f9228b4fa37910d0a`

### REQ-006

For the selected VOCC-oriented variant, the billing party issues demurrage and detention invoices within 30 calendar days from when charges were last incurred. Billed parties have at least 30 calendar days to make mitigation, refund, or waiver requests, and a timely request receives a resolution attempt within 30 calendar days unless both parties agree to a longer timeframe.

Basis: external_evidence

Observable: The environment displays the last-incurred charge date, invoice-issuance deadline, request deadline, response target, and any agreed extension as separate date facts.

Falsifiable consequence: A configured VOCC invoice or timely request whose externally evidenced deadline or response target is calculated with a different interval violates this capability.

Evidence: `E6` -> `source-revision-33fad34d48b676fa9f8d1b415c7f6dcbee67976d84b4302842a4ce4d43e0bd42/passage-ba0029aed22c4f2a09ab1efe4d64c1db7828315fef3931670ff2b3b2a252548e`, `E7` -> `source-revision-33fad34d48b676fa9f8d1b415c7f6dcbee67976d84b4302842a4ce4d43e0bd42/passage-1cef5b28518cb892497b70ca25d7b784470b7844dae49f9c069bf7316eda8b07`

## Workflows

### REQ-007

Submit a dispute against one or more invoice lines with a reason, asserted correction or requested waiver, submission timestamp, and zero or more supporting evidence records.

Basis: need

Observable: A valid submission creates a dispute record in Submitted status and records the selected line items, reason, requester, evidence references, and submission time.

Falsifiable consequence: A submission that does not create a traceable dispute record with the selected lines and submission timestamp fails the workflow.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Precondition: The invoice exists, is associated with the submitting party, contains at least one selected line, and the submission timestamp is no later than the configured synthetic dispute deadline.

Postcondition: One new dispute exists in Submitted status; the invoice and its charge lines are unchanged; all supplied evidence is linked to the new dispute.

### REQ-008

Validate a submitted dispute for invoice identity, billed-party authority, selected line existence, date and amount consistency, reason presence, and evidence linkage.

Basis: need

Observable: The environment reports validation findings and transitions a valid dispute to Under Review or an invalid dispute to Rejected.

Falsifiable consequence: A dispute with a missing invoice, nonexistent line, unauthorized requester, or malformed charge assertion reaching Under Review violates the workflow.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Precondition: A dispute is in Submitted status and its referenced invoice is present in the current world.

Postcondition: The dispute has a recorded validation result and status; no validation result silently changes the invoice amount, charge period, or supporting evidence.

### REQ-009

Resolve a timely dispute through a bounded review outcome: upheld, partially adjusted, waived, refunded, or denied. A timely request enters review and uses a 30-calendar-day synthetic resolution target unless the synthetic parties record an agreed extension.

Basis: need

Observable: The dispute timeline records review start, decision, decision reason, adjusted or refunded amount, response date, and any agreed extension.

Falsifiable consequence: A timely dispute with no extension and no resolution attempt by the configured synthetic 30-day target violates the workflow.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Precondition: The dispute is Under Review, the invoice and disputed lines remain available, and the reviewer has a permitted outcome.

Postcondition: The dispute reaches a terminal decision status; any amount adjustment is explicitly recorded against the affected line; unrelated invoice lines and evidence remain unchanged.

### REQ-010

Refuse a dispute submitted after the synthetic dispute deadline as late.

Basis: need

Observable: The submission response identifies the deadline, the evaluated submission time, and the reason LateDispute; no review record is created.

Falsifiable consequence: A late submission that appears in Submitted or Under Review status, or that changes invoice state, violates the workflow.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Precondition: The referenced invoice exists and the submission timestamp is later than the configured synthetic 30-calendar-day dispute deadline.

Postcondition: No dispute is created; the invoice, line items, amounts, charge periods, evidence, and statuses are semantically unchanged except for an allowed audit entry recording the refusal.

### REQ-011

Refuse invalid disputes, including unknown invoice or line, missing required reason, unauthorized billed party, contradictory dates, unsupported amount assertions, duplicate active dispute, or evidence attached to a nonexistent object.

Basis: need

Observable: The response returns one or more stable validation codes and identifies the failed field or relationship.

Falsifiable consequence: An invalid request that mutates invoice totals, creates a partial dispute, or changes an unrelated status violates the workflow.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Precondition: At least one validation predicate fails before dispute acceptance.

Postcondition: No domain object is created or modified, apart from an explicitly permitted refusal audit event; the refusal contains no implicit correction or partial persistence.

### REQ-012

Reset the environment to its named initial scenario and run all workflows locally without contacting real carrier, terminal, customs, payment, or tracking systems.

Basis: need

Observable: Reset produces the same world fingerprint for the same scenario and seed, and execution logs show no external-network dependency.

Falsifiable consequence: Two resets with the same scenario and seed producing different initial relations, or any workflow requiring a live carrier response, violates this workflow.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Precondition: The caller selects an available scenario and seed.

Postcondition: All synthetic records and relationships are restored to the scenario baseline; prior disputes, decisions, and mutations are absent; no external system has been contacted.

## Invariants

### REQ-013

Status transitions are monotonic within a dispute lifecycle: Submitted to Under Review to a terminal decision, or Submitted directly to Rejected. Terminal disputes cannot return to an active status.

Basis: need

Observable: Every status change is timestamped and represented in an ordered dispute history.

Falsifiable consequence: A terminal dispute returning to Submitted or Under Review is an invariant violation.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-014

Charge calculations are reproducible from stored free-time dates, charge-period dates, charge type, rate schedule, and any documented adjustment.

Basis: need

Observable: Recalculation produces the displayed line amount or identifies an explicit recorded adjustment.

Falsifiable consequence: The same stored inputs producing unexplained different amounts violate this invariant.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-015

The selected invoice variant exposes an understandable connection between the failure to pick up cargo or return equipment and the corresponding charge.

Basis: external_evidence

Observable: Each demurrage or detention line is traceable to the relevant pickup, terminal-stay, equipment-use, or return event and its charge period.

Falsifiable consequence: A charge line with no traceable operational event cannot be considered valid in the selected variant.

Evidence: `E2` -> `source-revision-33fad34d48b676fa9f8d1b415c7f6dcbee67976d84b4302842a4ce4d43e0bd42/passage-990308cba45a647da5b193866dd3e547f0822c58e206874f0996e23ce6fc9020`, `E22` -> `source-revision-c69e877f0163c7a05d481bd5bed2f2bcedff36a486bb1069452f8fcbce0f77fc/passage-39571c5d00423e89dd9e75d0f1a0d4c9ae8d92c6e2dd0e0552c2fdd3fa35a8e0`

### REQ-016

Reset isolation prevents data from one run, scenario, or seed from affecting another run.

Basis: need

Observable: After reset, no prior dispute, audit event, decision, or generated identifier remains unless it belongs to the selected baseline.

Falsifiable consequence: A prior run's dispute or mutation appearing after reset violates this invariant.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-017

The environment is synthetic and offline: all parties, identifiers, documents, events, rates, and correspondence are fabricated and no real carrier-system state is read or written.

Basis: need

Observable: The environment can be executed in an isolated setting with only its scenario inputs and local state.

Falsifiable consequence: A workflow that requires a real booking, carrier API, terminal feed, or external payment system violates this invariant.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

## Refusals

### REQ-018

Reject a late dispute with a stable LateDispute reason.

Basis: need

Observable: The caller receives a refusal containing invoice issue date, dispute deadline, submission time, and refusal code.

Falsifiable consequence: A late dispute entering the normal lifecycle is a failure.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Refusal condition: Submission time is later than the configured synthetic 30-calendar-day dispute deadline.

Prohibited mutation: Do not create a dispute, change invoice or line status, alter amounts or charge periods, attach evidence, or create a review task; only an explicitly permitted refusal audit event may be recorded.

### REQ-019

Reject invalid dispute payloads or relationships before acceptance.

Basis: need

Observable: The refusal identifies deterministic validation codes and leaves the domain snapshot unchanged.

Falsifiable consequence: Any partial object, amount change, or status transition after invalid submission is a failure.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Refusal condition: Any required field, authority relation, invoice-line relation, date relation, amount relation, or evidence relation is invalid.

Prohibited mutation: Do not create a dispute or modify any invoice, container, event, evidence record, or existing dispute.

### REQ-020

Reject an invoice configuration that assigns the same demurrage or detention invoice to multiple simultaneous billed parties.

Basis: external_evidence

Observable: Validation returns a MultipleBilledParties refusal before invoice acceptance.

Falsifiable consequence: An invoice with multiple simultaneous billed parties being accepted contradicts the selected rule basis.

Evidence: `E1` -> `source-revision-33fad34d48b676fa9f8d1b415c7f6dcbee67976d84b4302842a4ce4d43e0bd42/passage-2209f389bad3b80f0df0770f9ca6981ade0f2342e1b3cd8f9228b4fa37910d0a`

Refusal condition: More than one billed party is assigned to the invoice at the same time.

Prohibited mutation: Do not issue or activate the invoice, create charge obligations, or create a dispute against the invalid invoice.

### REQ-021

Refuse unsupported live-system operations.

Basis: need

Observable: The operation returns OfflineSyntheticOnly and identifies the prohibited external dependency.

Falsifiable consequence: The environment contacting a carrier, terminal, customs, payment, or tracking system violates the requirement.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

Refusal condition: An operation requests real external data retrieval, real invoice submission, real payment, or real carrier-system mutation.

Prohibited mutation: Do not open a network session, transmit identifiers or documents, persist an external response, or alter local domain state as a side effect.

## Initial-world requirements

### REQ-022

Provide a named baseline scenario containing at least one valid timely dispute, one late dispute candidate, and one invalid dispute candidate, all linked to meaningful synthetic shipment activity.

Basis: need

Observable: The baseline includes multiple containers and invoices with distinct charge types, free-time intervals, terminal or equipment events, evidence records, billed parties, and dates positioned before, on, and after the synthetic dispute deadline.

Falsifiable consequence: If reset cannot exercise at least one successful submission and both late and invalid refusal paths, the baseline is insufficient.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-023

The baseline includes at least one demurrage line whose charge period follows terminal free-time expiration and at least one detention line whose charge period follows equipment free-time expiration or late return.

Basis: need

Observable: The initial invoice views show the events, free-time dates, chargeable dates, rates, and amounts needed to reproduce both calculations.

Falsifiable consequence: A baseline containing only generic invoice records without exercisable demurrage and detention timing relations fails this condition.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

### REQ-024

The baseline includes evidence that supports different outcomes, such as a terminal availability or appointment interruption supporting mitigation and a timely pickup or return record supporting denial.

Basis: need

Observable: Reviewers can select evidence and reach at least two distinct resolution outcomes without importing external documents.

Falsifiable consequence: If every initial dispute has identical evidence and only one possible outcome, the baseline is not meaningfully varied.

Evidence: original Need clause mapping

## Assumptions

- The selected jurisdictional variant is United States-facing and uses the FMC VOCC concepts only as a bounded reference model.
- The environment models import-container scenarios; export scenarios and non-US legal regimes are outside the selected baseline.
- The synthetic dispute deadline is configured as 30 calendar days from invoice issuance for baseline exercise. This is a Need-authorized environment rule and is not presented as an externally established universal rule.
- The externally evidenced 30-day VOCC invoice-issuance interval is measured from when charges were last incurred; it is distinct from the synthetic dispute deadline.
- The externally evidenced 30-day request and resolution periods are represented as timing facts, while the broader dispute status model and outcome taxonomy remain synthetic workflow choices.
- Dates use a single declared timezone and calendar-day arithmetic; holidays and business-day exceptions are excluded unless a scenario explicitly adds them.
- A dispute may cover multiple invoice lines, but every selected line must belong to the referenced invoice and container relationships must remain consistent.
- All evidence content is fabricated and has no legal or commercial effect.

## Alternatives

- A marine-terminal-operator billing variant could be modeled separately, with invoice timing measured from the last incurred charge.
- An NVOCC variant could be modeled separately, with its invoice timing measured from the issuance of the upstream invoice it received.
- A carrier-specific commercial workflow could use different deadlines, evidence requirements, escalation paths, or status names.
- A richer scenario could include export containers, transshipment, multiple terminals, negotiated free time, or business-day calendars.

## Exclusions

- No real carrier, terminal, customs, payment, tracking, or regulatory-system integration.
- No legal conclusion that a synthetic dispute is valid under a particular contract.
- No exhaustive taxonomy of shipping statuses, evidence types, rate structures, ports, carriers, or stakeholder roles.
- No requirement to reproduce any specific carrier's proprietary invoice layout or dispute portal.
- No automatic adjudication of factual credibility beyond deterministic consistency checks and selected synthetic review outcomes.
- No claim that the cited FMC passages establish the complete synthetic dispute-window rule, outcome taxonomy, or all detailed workflow fields.

## Contradictions

None disclosed.

## Open gaps

None.

entries.text: A key provision of this rule determines that demurrage or detention invoices can only be issued to either: (1) the person for whose account the billing party provide ocean transportation or storage of cargo and who contracted with the billing party for the ocean transportation or storage of cargo; or (2) the “consignee,” defined as “the ultimate recipient of the cargo; the person to whom final delivery of the cargo is to be made”. Demurrage and detention bills cannot be issued to multiple parties simultaneously.

The new rule will advance the Commission’s goal of promoting supply chain fluidity by ensuring a clear connection between the failure to pick-up cargo or return equipment in a timely manner and the appropriate fee. The rule ensures that billed parties understand the demurrage or detention invoices they receive by requiring certain identifiable information be included by the billing party on the invoice. Failing to include any of the required information in a detention or demurrage invoice eliminates any obligation of the billed party to pay the applicable charge. Of course, if an invoice does comply, a charged party does have an obligation to pay charges billed. The new rule will provide relief to parties who should never have received a bill for detention or demurrage.

A [Final Rule issued today](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/02/26/2024-02926/demurrage-and-detention-billing-requirements) by the Federal Maritime Commission establishes new requirements for how common carriers and marine terminal operators (MTOs) must bill for demurrage and detention charges, providing clarity on who can be billed, within what timeframe, and the process for disputing bills.
[Skip to content](https://www.fmc.gov/articles/fmc-publishes-final-rule-on-detention-and-demurrage-billing-practices/#wp--skip-link--target)
[Home](https://www.fmc.gov/) > [News Articles](https://www.fmc.gov/articles/) > FMC Publishes Final Rule on Detention and Demurrage Billing Practices

The rule also requires vessel-operating-common carriers (VOCCs) and MTOs to issue detention and demurrage invoices within 30 calendar days from when charges were last incurred. Non-vessel-operating common carriers must issue demurrage and detention invoices within 30 calendar days from the issuance date of the invoice they received.

Billed parties have at least 30 calendar days to make fee mitigation, refund, or waiver requests. If a timely filed request is made, the billing party must attempt to resolve the matter within 30 calendar days, unless both parties agree to a longer timeframe.

Most of the rule takes effect on May 28, 2024. The “Contents of Invoice” section 541.6 involves information collection and must be approved by the Office of Management and Budget. The Commission will announce the effective date of section 541.6 once approved.

The Commission’s current focus on issues related to detention and demurrage dates back to 2014 when the Commission hosted [multiple forums on maritime congestion](https://www.fmc.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/reportdemurrage.pdf). The feedback received from these forums was integrated into the 2015 FMC report, “[Rules, Rates, and Practices Relating to Detention, Demurrage, and Free Time for Containerized Imports and Exports Moving Through Selected United States Ports](https://www.fmc.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/reportdemurrage.pdf) [PDF, 367 KB] .”

These data are provided to the FMC, summarized, and then made available to the public for a general understanding of the scope of detention and demurrage billed by and paid to carriers. Detention is charged for extended use of intermodal equipment and demurrage accrues when a container exceeds free time on a marine terminal.

In 2018, Commissioner Rebecca Dye was named the investigative officer for [Fact Finding 28](https://www.fmc.gov/fact-finding-28/), which focused on the impact of detention and demurrage on supply chain efficiency. Commissioner Dye issued multiple recommendations from this fact-finding, including a proposed interpretive rule on detention and demurrage under the Shipping Act. The NPRM for the interpretive rule received over 100 comments from the public and the [final rule was issued in May 2020](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2020/05/18/2020-09370/interpretive-rule-on-demurrage-and-detention-under-the-shipping-act).

The pandemic brought additional challenges to the supply chain and, in response, the Commission initiated [Fact Finding 29](https://www.fmc.gov/fact-finding-29/), again with Commissioner Rebecca Dye as investigative officer. While this fact finding centered on engagement with supply chain stakeholders to identify solutions to the pandemic’s disruption of the supply chain system, maritime congestion resulted in renewed attention on detention and demurrage.

_Faker_ is a Python package that generates fake data for you. Whether you need to bootstrap your database, create good-looking XML documents, fill-in your persistence to stress test it, or anonymize data taken from a production service, Faker is for you.
Faker is heavily inspired by [PHP Faker](https://github.com/fzaninotto/Faker), [Perl Faker](https://metacpan.org/dist/Data-Faker), and by [Ruby Faker](https://github.com/stympy/faker).

This package was also previously called `fake-factory` which was already deprecated by the end of 2016, and much has changed since then, so please ensure that your project and its dependencies do not depend on the old package.
Use `faker.Faker()` to create and initialize a faker generator, which can generate data by accessing properties named after the type of data you want.

requirements.falsifiable_consequence: A late dispute entering the normal lifecycle is a failure.
requirements.observable_relation: The caller receives a refusal containing invoice issue date, dispute deadline, submission time, and refusal code.
requirements.prohibited_mutation: Do not create a dispute, change invoice or line status, alter amounts or charge periods, attach evidence, or create a review task; only an explicitly permitted refusal audit event may be recorded.
requirements.refusal_condition: Submission time is later than the configured synthetic 30-calendar-day dispute deadline.
requirements.state_relation: Reject a late dispute with a stable LateDispute reason.

requirements.falsifiable_consequence: Any partial object, amount change, or status transition after invalid submission is a failure.
requirements.observable_relation: The refusal identifies deterministic validation codes and leaves the domain snapshot unchanged.
requirements.prohibited_mutation: Do not create a dispute or modify any invoice, container, event, evidence record, or existing dispute.
requirements.refusal_condition: Any required field, authority relation, invoice-line relation, date relation, amount relation, or evidence relation is invalid.
requirements.state_relation: Reject invalid dispute payloads or relationships before acceptance.

requirements.falsifiable_consequence: An invoice with multiple simultaneous billed parties being accepted contradicts the selected rule basis.
requirements.observable_relation: Validation returns a MultipleBilledParties refusal before invoice acceptance.
requirements.prohibited_mutation: Do not issue or activate the invoice, create charge obligations, or create a dispute against the invalid invoice.
requirements.refusal_condition: More than one billed party is assigned to the invoice at the same time.
requirements.state_relation: Reject an invoice configuration that assigns the same demurrage or detention invoice to multiple simultaneous billed parties.

requirements.falsifiable_consequence: The environment contacting a carrier, terminal, customs, payment, or tracking system violates the requirement.
requirements.observable_relation: The operation returns OfflineSyntheticOnly and identifies the prohibited external dependency.
requirements.prohibited_mutation: Do not open a network session, transmit identifiers or documents, persist an external response, or alter local domain state as a side effect.
requirements.refusal_condition: An operation requests real external data retrieval, real invoice submission, real payment, or real carrier-system mutation.
requirements.state_relation: Refuse unsupported live-system operations.

assumptions: The selected jurisdictional variant is United States-facing and uses the FMC VOCC concepts only as a bounded reference model.
The environment models import-container scenarios; export scenarios and non-US legal regimes are outside the selected baseline.

The synthetic dispute deadline is configured as 30 calendar days from invoice issuance for baseline exercise. This is a Need-authorized environment rule and is not presented as an externally established universal rule.
The externally evidenced 30-day VOCC invoice-issuance interval is measured from when charges were last incurred; it is distinct from the synthetic dispute deadline.
The externally evidenced 30-day request and resolution periods are represented as timing facts, while the broader dispute status model and outcome taxonomy remain synthetic workflow choices.
Dates use a single declared timezone and calendar-day arithmetic; holidays and business-day exceptions are excluded unless a scenario explicitly adds them.
A dispute may cover multiple invoice lines, but every selected line must belong to the referenced invoice and container relationships must remain consistent.
All evidence content is fabricated and has no legal or commercial effect.
exclusions: No real carrier, terminal, customs, payment, tracking, or regulatory-system integration.
No legal conclusion that a synthetic dispute is valid under a particular contract.
No exhaustive taxonomy of shipping statuses, evidence types, rate structures, ports, carriers, or stakeholder roles.
No requirement to reproduce any specific carrier's proprietary invoice layout or dispute portal.
No automatic adjudication of factual credibility beyond deterministic consistency checks and selected synthetic review outcomes.
No claim that the cited FMC passages establish the complete synthetic dispute-window rule, outcome taxonomy, or all detailed workflow fields.
residual_limitations: The evidence set supports selected FMC timing and billing concepts but does not establish an exhaustive legal regime, complete invoice-content rule, universal dispute-window rule, or carrier-specific workflow taxonomy; the Brief expressly treats those as bounded or synthetic choices.

Federal Register source access is represented by access-block and CAPTCHA passages, so the review relies on the extracted FMC passages supplied in the bounded evidence rather than independently inspecting the linked final rule.
The Brief does not claim exhaustive coverage of shipping statuses, evidence types, rates, ports, carriers, stakeholder roles, or proprietary carrier workflows.
selected_world.scope: A bounded United States synthetic environment centered on a vessel-operating common carrier (VOCC) billing a consignee for import demurrage and detention. The environment uses a fixed synthetic calendar, deterministic seed, fabricated carrier and terminal identities, and local-only state. It models a normal dispute lifecycle with a synthetic 30-calendar-day dispute window and a separate 30-calendar-day resolution target for timely requests. The externally evidenced timing facts are limited to VOCC invoice issuance and the FMC-described request and resolution periods; the exact synthetic dispute-window anchor is a disclosed Need-authorized workflow choice, not a claim that all carriers or jurisdictions use identical commercial rules.

clause_findings.rationale: The Brief defines a resettable synthetic domain with actors, invoices, containers, charge periods, operational events, and linked supporting evidence.
The Brief specifies submission, validation, review, resolution, timing rules, ordered status transitions, and observable timeline data.
The Brief defines deterministic refusal of late and invalid disputes and enumerates prohibited mutations, allowing only explicitly permitted refusal-audit entries.
The Brief specifies named seeded scenarios, deterministic reset behavior, fabricated initial data, local-only execution, and refusal of live-system operations.

The requirement's external basis is valid. E1 states that demurrage or detention invoices may be issued to an eligible billed party or consignee and cannot be issued to multiple parties simultaneously; the consignee definition also supports the stated ultimate-recipient modeling.

The requirement's external basis is valid. E6 supports the VOCC 30-calendar-day invoice-issuance interval measured from the last incurred charge, and E7 supports at least 30 days for requests and a 30-day resolution attempt absent an agreed extension.

This is a valid Need-based offline constraint and the Brief specifies refusal of live retrieval, submission, payment, or carrier-system mutation without network or local side effects.

scope_assessment.rationale: The Brief discloses a coherent United States-facing, VOCC-oriented import-container baseline, a synthetic 30-calendar-day dispute window, a separate externally evidenced invoice-issuance interval, fixed calendar handling, and local-only execution. It expressly identifies alternative MTO, NVOCC, carrier-specific, export, transshipment, and richer-calendar variants as outside the selected baseline rather than silently narrowing the Need.
